guides.definition: Creates a SourceFile syntax tree from TypeScript or JavaScript text.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: The logical source-file name and extension.

parameters.name: sourceText
parameters.description: The text to parse.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The ScriptTarget enum member used by the parser.

parameters.name: setParents
parameters.description: Whether parsed nodes receive parent links.

examples.title: Parse a typed binding
examples.explanation: The returned SourceFile owns the parsed statement tree and optional parent links.

guides.definition: Builds the compiler's whole-project view from root files, options, and an optional host.

parameters.name: rootNames
parameters.description: An array of source file paths.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: CompilerOptions controlling resolution, checking, and emit.

examples.title: Create a strict no-emit program
examples.explanation: Program coordinates source loading, binding, type checking, module resolution, and emit state.

guides.definition: Visits a node's syntactic children in source order through the supported traversal API.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The AST node whose children are visited.

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Work performed for each child.

examples.title: List source-file child kinds
examples.explanation: forEachChild exposes the public syntactic tree without relying on internal node arrays.

guides.definition: Creates a synthesized Identifier through the supported node factory.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The identifier's source spelling.

examples.title: Create an answer identifier
examples.explanation: Using ts.factory keeps synthesized nodes compatible with the active compiler version.

guides.definition: Performs syntactic transformation and emit for one source string without creating a complete Program.

parameters.name: sourceText
parameters.description: The isolated TypeScript source to transpile.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The emitted JavaScript language level.

parameters.name: moduleKind
parameters.description: The emitted module format.

examples.title: Strip a number annotation
examples.explanation: transpileModule emits JavaScript but does not perform whole-program semantic checking.

guides.definition: Creates a Printer that converts parsed or synthesized nodes back into source text.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Formatting and newline settings for emitted text.

examples.title: Create a line-feed printer
examples.explanation: The printer can render individual nodes, node lists, or complete files with consistent formatting options.

guides.definition: Renders a node to source text using an emit hint and source-file context.

parameters.name: printer
parameters.description: A ts.Printer expression.

parameters.name: hint
parameters.description: How the printer should interpret the node's syntactic role.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The AST node to render.

parameters.name: sourceFile
parameters.description: The source context used by the printer.

examples.title: Print a synthesized identifier
examples.explanation: The printer renders the factory-created identifier as valid source text.

guides.definition: Applies one or more transformer factories to a node or node array and returns transformed roots.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The node or node array to transform.

parameters.name: transformer
parameters.description: A TransformerFactory compatible with the source node type.
parameters.defaultValue: context => root => ts.visitEachChild(root, node => node, context)

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Work performed with result.transformed.

examples.title: Run an identity transform
examples.explanation: TransformationResult owns disposable compiler resources and exposes the transformed roots.

guides.definition: Visits child nodes through a transformer context and rebuilds parents only when descendants change.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The active TransformationContext supplied to a transformer factory.

examples.title: Define a recursive transformer visitor
examples.explanation: visitEachChild preserves unchanged nodes and uses the transformation context for safe tree updates.

guides.definition: Builds the file-system and output callbacks a Program uses for source loading and emit.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Options shared by the host and Program.

parameters.name: setParents
parameters.description: Whether host-created source files should include parent links.

examples.title: Create a strict analysis host
examples.explanation: The returned host can be wrapped to customize source reads, module resolution, or emitted outputs.

guides.definition: Returns the semantic engine used to resolve symbols and inspect types within a Program.

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: The compiler Program that owns semantic state.

examples.title: Access semantic analysis
examples.explanation: A TypeChecker is tied to its Program and should be used with nodes from that same program.

guides.definition: Returns the semantic Type associated with a node in the current Program.

parameters.name: checker
parameters.description: The Program's TypeChecker.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: A node belonging to the checker's Program.

examples.title: Inspect a declaration type
examples.code:
const type = checker.getTypeAtLocation(node);
console.log(checker.typeToString(type));
examples.explanation: The Type object represents the checker's semantic interpretation at that source location.

guides.definition: Finds the declaration symbol referenced or introduced at a node when one exists.

parameters.name: checker
parameters.description: The Program's TypeChecker.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: An identifier or other symbol-bearing node.

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Work performed when resolution succeeds.

examples.title: Read a resolved symbol name
examples.code:
const symbol = checker.getSymbolAtLocation(node);
if (symbol) console.log(symbol.getName());
examples.explanation: Symbols represent the type system's view of declarations and references, not JavaScript Symbol values.

guides.definition: Converts a Type object into a readable TypeScript type expression.

parameters.name: checker
parameters.description: The TypeChecker that owns the Type.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The semantic Type to format.

parameters.name: enclosingNode
parameters.description: Optional context for accessible names.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: TypeFormatFlags controlling detail and spelling.

examples.title: Print a complete type
examples.code:
const text = checker.typeToString(type, undefined, ts.TypeFormatFlags.NoTruncation);
console.log(text);
examples.explanation: Formatting through the owning checker respects aliases, scope, and requested detail flags.

guides.definition: Combines configuration, syntactic, options, global, and semantic diagnostics for a Program.

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: The Program to diagnose.

examples.title: Collect project diagnostics
examples.explanation: The helper gathers the standard diagnostic phases typically checked before calling emit.

guides.definition: Converts nested diagnostic message chains into one readable string with a chosen newline.

parameters.name: messageText
parameters.description: A diagnostic string or DiagnosticMessageChain.

parameters.name: newLine
parameters.description: The separator used between nested messages.

examples.title: Format a compiler diagnostic
examples.code:
import * as ts from "@typescript/typescript6";
console.log(ts.flattenDiagnosticMessageText(diagnostic.messageText, "\n"));
examples.explanation: Nested explanatory branches become a stable multiline message suitable for a console or problem list.

guides.definition: Maps a zero-based source offset to its zero-based line and character coordinates.

parameters.name: sourceFile
parameters.description: The SourceFileLike containing the position.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: A zero-based character offset.

examples.title: Locate a diagnostic
examples.explanation: Adding one produces the one-based coordinates commonly shown to users.

guides.definition: Writes JavaScript, declaration, and source-map outputs according to compiler options and callbacks.

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: The Program to emit.

parameters.name: sourceFile
parameters.description: A specific SourceFile or undefined for the entire Program.

parameters.name: writeFile
parameters.description: An optional callback that receives generated outputs.

examples.title: Emit all program outputs
examples.code:
const emitResult = program.emit();
console.log(emitResult.emitSkipped, emitResult.diagnostics.length);
examples.explanation: EmitResult reports whether output was skipped and includes diagnostics produced during emit.

guides.definition: Walks upward from a search path until a named configuration file is found.

parameters.name: searchPath
parameters.description: The file or directory where the upward search begins.

parameters.name: configName
parameters.description: The configuration filename to locate.

examples.title: Locate tsconfig.json
examples.explanation: The search uses the compiler system's fileExists callback and returns undefined when no config is found.

guides.definition: Loads JSON configuration text and reports a structured config value or a diagnostic.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: The tsconfig or jsconfig file to read.

examples.title: Read tsconfig.json
examples.explanation: readConfigFile handles comments and compiler JSON syntax while preserving parse errors as diagnostics.

guides.definition: Expands a config object into file names, normalized compiler options, project references, and diagnostics.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The value returned by readConfigFile or another JSON source.

parameters.name: basePath
parameters.description: The directory used to resolve relative paths and include patterns.

examples.title: Resolve a configuration object
examples.explanation: The returned ParsedCommandLine contains normalized options and the resolved project file list.

guides.definition: Reads a config file and resolves its options and file graph through a ParseConfigFileHost.

parameters.name: configPath
parameters.description: The configuration file to load.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Compiler options that override or extend the config.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: A ParseConfigFileHost used for filesystem access and error reporting.

examples.title: Load tsconfig through a host
examples.explanation: This higher-level helper combines config reading, extends resolution, path expansion, and option conversion.

guides.definition: Runs TypeScript's module-resolution algorithm for a specifier and containing file.

parameters.name: moduleName
parameters.description: The import specifier to resolve.

parameters.name: containingFile
parameters.description: The absolute or project-relative source file issuing the import.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Module and path settings used by resolution.

examples.title: Resolve a relative dependency
examples.explanation: The result includes the resolved module when successful and failed lookup locations for diagnostics or tracing.

guides.definition: Creates a builder that can reuse semantic and emit state between related compilations.

parameters.name: rootNames
parameters.description: The source files entering the project graph.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Incremental compiler options, commonly including incremental and tsBuildInfoFile.

examples.title: Create an incremental analysis build
examples.explanation: Builder programs expose the underlying Program and reuse prior work when supplied compatible state.

guides.definition: Tracks affected files so semantic diagnostics and emit can be updated incrementally.

parameters.name: rootNames
parameters.description: The source files entering the builder graph.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Options shared across builder updates.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: An optional CompilerHost or BuilderProgramHost.

examples.title: Create an affected-file builder
examples.explanation: The builder can report and emit only files affected by changes when reused by a watch or incremental workflow.

guides.definition: Creates the host callbacks and builder strategy used to monitor a TypeScript project configuration.

parameters.name: configPath
parameters.description: The tsconfig file to watch.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Compiler options layered over the configuration.

examples.title: Prepare a semantic watch host
examples.explanation: The host can be customized before it is passed to createWatchProgram.

guides.definition: Starts file watching and rebuilds a project through the supplied watch host.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: A host created or customized for the watched project.

examples.title: Start a config watch
examples.explanation: The returned watch owns file watchers and the current builder program and should be closed when no longer needed.

guides.definition: Tests a Node's syntax kind and exposes Identifier-specific members to TypeScript.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The AST node to test.

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Work performed with the narrowed Identifier.

examples.title: Read identifier text
examples.code:
import * as ts from "@typescript/typescript6";
if (ts.isIdentifier(node)) console.log(node.text);
examples.explanation: The predicate narrows node to ts.Identifier inside the branch.

guides.definition: Tests whether a Node is a function declaration and enables access to its name, parameters, and body.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The AST node to test.

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Work performed with the narrowed function declaration.

examples.title: Read a function name
examples.code:
import * as ts from "@typescript/typescript6";
if (ts.isFunctionDeclaration(node)) console.log(node.name?.text);
examples.explanation: The supported predicate is safer than manually comparing SyntaxKind and casting.

guides.definition: Tests whether a Node is a class declaration and exposes its class-specific syntax members.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The AST node to test.

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Work performed with the narrowed class declaration.

examples.title: Inspect a class declaration
examples.code:
import * as ts from "@typescript/typescript6";
if (ts.isClassDeclaration(node)) console.log(node.name?.text, node.members.length);
examples.explanation: The predicate narrows node to ts.ClassDeclaration for safe member access.

guides.definition: Returns a bitmask containing the modifier flags associated with a declaration.

parameters.name: declaration
parameters.description: The declaration whose modifiers are inspected.

examples.title: Check whether a declaration is exported
examples.explanation: Bitwise checks test individual ModifierFlags without depending on modifier-array layout.

guides.definition: Returns JSDoc blocks and tags associated with a host syntax node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The syntax node whose documentation is requested.

examples.title: Count documentation nodes
examples.explanation: The helper handles JSDoc attachment rules and returns syntax nodes for structured inspection.

guides.definition: Returns the compiler installation path to the default lib declaration selected by compiler options.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Options whose target influences the selected default library.

examples.title: Locate the ES2022 default library
examples.code:
import * as ts from "@typescript/typescript6";
console.log(ts.getDefaultLibFilePath({ target: ts.ScriptTarget.ES2022 }));
examples.explanation: The returned path points into the active TypeScript package rather than the user's project source tree.
